scope: Image pricing strategy and staged Stripe catalog entries for Creator, Studio, and Team.

research.finding: A familiar ladder separates plans by explicit usage and privacy/concurrency terms; GALX must not copy unsupported modes or promises.
Plain-language usage balances and reset expectations are easier to compare than opaque job labels; GALX will add those only with enforceable accounting.
Stripe supports recurring Prices with lookup keys and an active flag; inactive Prices are appropriate for a catalog staged before checkout.

strategy.current_offer: Start free plus GALX Pro at the existing published $10/month contract.

guardrails: Products and Prices are inactive and have checkoutEnabled=false.
No customers, subscriptions, payments, tax registrations, migrations, or entitlements were created.
The current Pro Product and Price were not modified.
Private mode remains an owner-scoped product control, not a plan entitlement.
Higher usage, throughput, seats, roles, support, video, editing and priority are release gates, not current promises.
verification: The provisioning command uses deterministic Product IDs, lookup keys, metadata and idempotency keys.
Live Stripe readback confirmed three staged Products and recurring Prices with active=false.

A separate read-only audit found the existing GALX Pro lookup key active at $20 with no matching subscriptions in the bounded account scan; the repository's published Pro contract remains $10 and was intentionally not changed in this pass.
No secret, customer data or webhook payload was recorded in this evidence.
limits: This change stages a catalog for pricing review; it does not make the new plans purchasable or change runtime access.
